✓ Wular Lake.fact: Wular Lake (Urdu pronunciation: [ʋʊlər]), also known as Wolar (Kashmiri pronunciation: [ʋɔlar]) in Kashmiri, is one of the largest freshwater lakes in the Indian subcontinent. The lake basin was formed as a result of tectonic activity and is fed by the Jhelum River and the streams Madhumati and Arin.  The lake's size varies seasonally from 30 to 189 square kilometres.  In addition, much of the lake has been drained as a result of willow plantations being built on the shore in the 1950s.  == Background == === Etymology === In ancient times, Wular Lake was also called Mahapadmasar (Sanskrit: महापद्मसरः)

The origin may also be attributed to a Kashmiri word 'Wul', which means a gap or a fissure, an appellation that must have come also during this period.
